task.title: Stash Changes
task.shortdesc: Shelve your current changes so you can switch context, then bring them back later.

context.p: A stash sets your uncommitted changes aside and returns the working copy to a clean state. Use it when you need to switch context, such as before switching branches, pulling remote changes, or starting another task before you are ready to commit. Your changes wait in the stash until you apply them again.
context.note: If your working copy has a file system name collision (for example, two files whose names differ only in letter case on a case-insensitive file system), stashing is refused, and so are the pull and pre-push operations that stash internally. Resolve the collision before you stash. See .

step.cmd: On the toolbar, open the drop-down and select Stash changes....

info.p: To stash only part of your work, select the files in the or area, right-click, and select Stash selected files.... This stashes the complete change of each selected file (both its staged and unstaged parts) and reverts those files to their last committed state, leaving every other change in the working copy untouched. The Include untracked option controls whether selected untracked files are included. If it is off and your selection contains only untracked files, nothing is stashed. The action is unavailable when the selection contains conflicts.
info.note: Because a partial stash is carried out in several steps, the Git Client first saves a full backup stash labeled Backup created while stashing selected files. If the operation fails partway, your working copy may be left partially modified. To recover, open the stashes dialog box, apply that backup stash, and then delete it.

step.cmd:
To bring a stash back, open the
drop-down and select List stashes....

info.p: In the Stashes dialog box, Apply restores the selected stash, Delete removes it, and Delete all clears every stash. Select Delete stash after being applied to remove a stash automatically once it is applied. Applying a stash can produce conflicts, which you can resolve as described in .
